name: Basilique Notre Dame d'Afrique
description: Basilica in Algiers overlooking the bay of the capital city. Completed in 1872, this splendid building of neo-bysantine architecture is ornately decorated in the inside in the Spanish-Moorish decor. Unique in its genre, it is probably one of the only churches in the world where the invocation to the Virgin Mary, Our Lady of Africa reads "Notre Dame d'Afrique, priez pour nous et pour les musulmans - Our Lady of Africa, pray for us and for Muslims". It is dear to the Algerian people who see it as 'their' church. PLEASE NOTE - Appropriate dress required to enter the Basilica

name: Le Jardin d'Essai du Hamma
description: The Botanical Garden of Algiers, Algeria History of the Garden In 1831, the French colony began undertaking remediation work on the marshlands in order to cultivate agricultural soil. By 1832, Governor General Antoine Avisard signed a decree that established a test garden in a place called El Hamma, east of Algiers. El Hamma provided a perfect plot for the agricultural plans due to its richness in water and cool climate near the sea. The aim of the garden was to serve as both a model farm and a test garden to install, acclimate and study various imported plant species. The garden’s main function in the beginning was diffusing useful plants for medicinal, economic and commercial purposes before scientific and horticultural activities were adopted. The zoological garden was created in 1900, under the initiative of Dr Joseph Ange who was the correspondent of the Paris Museum. name: National Museum of Antiquities of Algiers
description: Discover the millennial history of art in Algeria at the National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Arts. Inaugurated in 1897, this museum located in the Freedom Park (formerly Galland Park) in Algiers is the oldest in Algeria and Africa. It invites you to explore a vast collection of classical antiquities and Islamic art objects from the various Arab-Muslim dynasties that exercised power in Algeria, the Maghreb, and the Middle East. The museum's collection includes a variety of works, such as ceramics, paintings, sculptures, pottery, textiles, archaeological objects, and art pieces in different materials. Prepare to be amazed by this unique overview of art in Algeria.
